title: Her grandson resembles Jelly; family photographs
summary: Her grandson's playing sounds like Jelly's; she shows pictures of grandchildren and son and buys a piano.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I'm going to tell you what, and he and my brother play in Chicago. My little grandchild had that first deliverance over the keys, you know. Sounds so much like jelly, and you'd be surprised at the resemblance. Wait, let me show you his picture.

My—my grandson's picture. I have these two large pictures that look just like— Of your grandson. My grandson. Look like more than my son did. Oh, yeah. When he was a little boy. It's a nice picture. This is my granddaughter. But that's the one that's married. Oh, yes. Oh, yeah. That's a girl up now. That's my son. My son's a nice-looking— Yes. A nice-looking young son. I hate to say that because he looks so much like me.
No, but he is. He's a good-looking.

And I have nothing to be proud of him because he's never given me a day's trouble. What kind of a piano did your brother have in Chicago? A baby grand. A baby grand. A baby grand. A baby grand. I bought my little grandson, uh— Waitel, I think it is. I bought my son's instruments when he was a little boy. And he looked up to that account for my whole— that long time ago, and my sales letter, Miss Burke, she said, I said, all of you can have anything you want right here in the store. So later on, I got this machine over there after I paid for the piano. Because they gave him lessons for a year with the piano. And then whatever you paid on the lessons in the piano, they added to the account when you bought a new piano. So we bought a new French piano because his mother has French Spanish in our home.
